decks.notes: This Vintage 1 vs 1 deck is an Oath of Druids Control archetype. The main goal of the deck is to use Oath of Druids to cheat powerful creatures into play, while controlling the game with counterspells and disruption spells. It includes powerful cards like Ancestral Recall, Black Lotus, and Moxes for fast mana acceleration. Show and Tell and Tinker are included as additional ways to cheat creatures into play. The deck also includes various tutors and card draw spells to provide consistency. Additionally, the deck has some planeswalkers like Oko, Thief of Crowns to further control the game and Atraxa, Grand Unifier for potent abilities.

This vintage 1 vs 1 deck revolves around using the powerful combo card Doomsday to set up a winning sequence of cards. The deck includes cards like Ancestral Recall, Black Lotus, and Time Walk for card advantage and acceleration, along with various tutors and counterspells to protect the combo. By carefully managing resources and utilizing cards like Necropotence and Thassa's Oracle, this deck aims to quickly assemble its combo pieces and win the game in a single explosive turn.

This deck aims to generate a high amount of mana quickly using powerful mana artifacts and spells like Dark Ritual, Sol Ring, and Black Lotus. The player then uses card draw spells and tutors to assemble the necessary combo pieces, such as Time Vault and Voltaic Key, to generate a large storm count. Finally, the player cast Tendrils of Agony to deal a lethal amount of damage to the opponent in a single turn. The deck also includes disruption spells like Force of Will to protect its combo and control the game.

The deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's game plan with hatebears like Thalia, Guardian of Thraben and Chancellor of the Annex while also applying pressure with aggressive creatures like Archon of Emeria and White Plume Adventurer. It aims to slow down the opponent's spells with cards like Trinisphere and Wasteland while also disrupting their mana base. By combining disruptive elements with aggressive creatures, the deck aims to control the game and win through incremental advantage and efficient threats.

This deck focuses on efficiently casting multiple spells in a single turn to generate a high storm count and win the game with Tendrils of Agony. The deck includes powerful combo pieces like Yawgmoth's Will, Tinker, and Bolas's Citadel, along with fast mana sources like Black Lotus and Moxen to help accelerate its game plan. The inclusion of protection spells like Force of Will and Flusterstorm helps to protect the combo pieces from disruption, allowing the deck to execute its game plan smoothly and efficiently. It aims to win the game through a quick and explosive combo finish.

This Vintage 1 vs 1 Combo deck revolves around utilizing Coveted Jewel to generate mana and card advantage, while also utilizing powerful artifacts such as Time Vault, Tinker, and Mana Crypt. The deck aims to control the board with counter spells like Force of Will and Trinisphere, while also utilizing cards like Paradoxical Outcome to draw into key pieces of the combo. With cards like Urza's Saga and Karn, the Great Creator to tutor for artifacts and disrupt the opponent's game plan, this deck aims to assemble its combo pieces quickly and win the game efficiently.

The deck focuses on utilizing powerful cards to control the game, such as Ancestral Recall, Force of Will, and Demonic Tutor, while also utilizing key artifacts like Time Vault and Manifold Key to create an unbeatable lock. The deck aims to disrupt the opponent's game plan with counterspells and removal spells, while also generating card advantage with cantrips like Brainstorm and Ponder. By efficiently managing resources and disrupting the opponent's strategy, the deck aims to outlast and outlast the opponent until victory.

This vintage 1 vs 1 deck focuses on controlling the game through a combination of counter spells, card advantage, and disruptive creatures. The deck aims to disrupt the opponent's game plan while advancing its own win condition, which includes utilizing key artifacts like Time Vault and Bolas's Citadel. The deck also leverages powerful tutors and card draw spells to find crucial pieces quickly. With a strong mana base and versatile answers to threats, this Esper Control deck aims to outmaneuver opponents and secure victory through careful, strategic plays.

The main concept of this deck is to utilize the Dredge mechanic to quickly fill the graveyard with creature cards, allowing for explosive plays and graveyard synergies. By stocking the graveyard with cards like Golgari Grave-Troll and Stinkweed Imp, the deck can consistently bring back threats like Ichorid and Prized Amalgam. Cards like Bridge from Below and Cabal Therapy further enhance the graveyard strategy, while Force of Will provides protection and disruption. Overall, the deck aims to overwhelm the opponent with a combination of graveyard recursion and powerful creatures.

The deck focuses on aggressive plays with hatebear creatures like Thalia and Archon of Emeria to slow down opponents, while also utilizing cards like Chancellor of the Annex and Trinisphere to disrupt their game plan. The deck also includes powerful removal in the form of Solitude and versatile threats like White Plume Adventurer and Seasoned Dungeoneer. The mana base is streamlined for efficiency and consistency, allowing the deck to apply pressure early and maintain control throughout the game.

The deck focuses on playing aggressive creatures while also disrupting the opponent's game plan with Hatebear cards like Thalia and Archon of Emeria. It also includes artifact hate with Force of Vigor and Chalice of the Void, as well as equipment like Batterskull and Kaldra Compleat to further pressure the opponent. The mana base is designed to support the aggressive strategy with efficient fixing and disruption options like Strip Mine and Karakas. Overall, the deck aims to apply early pressure while slowing down the opponent's game plan with disruptive elements.

This deck focuses on assembling the combo pieces needed to generate large amounts of mana and draw cards with cards like Paradoxical Outcome. The deck is designed to ramp quickly and assemble powerful artifacts like Coveted Jewel and Time Vault with cards like Tinker and Trinisphere. By utilizing Urza's Saga and Mishra's Workshop, the deck can efficiently find and play these key pieces while also disrupting the opponent's game plan with counterspells like Force of Will. The goal is to outpace the opponent and win the game through overwhelming advantage and powerful combos.

The deck focuses on utilizing Oath of Druids to cheat powerful creatures into play, such as Atraxa, Grand Unifier, Narset, Parter of Veils and Oko, Thief of Crowns. It includes various tutors and card selection spells to find key pieces, as well as counter spells like Force of Will to protect the combo. Additionally, it has a disruptive element with cards like Spell Pierce and Flusterstorm to control the opponent's plays. The mana base is optimized for consistency and includes powerful artifacts like Black Lotus and Moxen for fast mana acceleration.

This deck revolves around using Coveted Jewel as a key combo piece to generate mana and draw cards with Paradoxical Outcome. Tolarian Academy, Grim Monolith, and Mishra's Workshop help ramp up mana quickly. Cards like Trinisphere and Force of Will provide interaction and protection. The deck also has alternate win conditions with Time Vault and Karn, the Great Creator. Mystic Forge and Urza's Saga provide additional card advantage and recursion abilities. Overall, the deck aims to create explosive turns and outvalue the opponent through synergy and powerful artifacts.

This Vintage 1 vs 1 Esper Control deck focuses on utilizing powerful control cards like Force of Will, Swords to Plowshares, and Force of Negation to disrupt the opponent's game plan while assembling a dominating late-game board presence. With a mix of efficient removal, card draw, and counterspells, the deck aims to control the pace of the game and outvalue the opponent. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion adds additional value and resilience to the deck's game plan, providing a consistent source of recurring threats and card advantage.

The deck focuses on disrupting opponents' strategies with aggressive hatebears while also utilizing powerful artifacts and mana acceleration to establish early board presence and pressure. With a mix of disruptive creatures like Thalia and Chancellor of the Annex, along with powerful artifacts like Trinisphere and Moxen, the deck aims to slow down opponents and control the game. By combining hate cards with aggressive creatures, the deck can disrupt opponents' plans while applying pressure to win the game quickly.
